In summary, our research is concerned with

the role of free-volume defects in the microstructure of ion-conducting glasses and shows that the presence of the free-volume defects in glasses is an important factor determining their microhardness.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the free-volume defects are responsible for both the microstructure of a glass and its ion conductivity.
the presence of the free-volume defects with the size of about 0.4 nm is responsible for the load-independent indentation hardness of the Ag/AgI-modified As 2 S3 glasses.
the free-volume defects with the volume of the Ag + ion size are the main structural defects responsible for the ion conduction in the Ag/AgI-modified As 2 S3 glasses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the free-volume defects in the structure of glass are responsible for the observed decrease in H V with increasing load P and that the load-independent indentation hardness H 0 can be considered a measure of the free-volume defects.

free-volume defects in the structure of As 2 S glasses are responsible for the formation of the AgI nanoclusters, the formation of which is responsible for the increase in the microhardness H V of the Ag-modified As 2 S glass with the applied load P.
the PALS and the load dependent Vickers hardness measurements can be used together to study free-volume defects in glassy systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PALS and microhardness data can be applied together to study the structure and microstructure of glasses.
the positron annihilation spectroscopy and microhardness data can be used as a complementary technique to study the free-volume defects in glassy materials.
the PALS and indentation hardness measurements can be used to characterize the free-volume defects in glassy materials.
